subject: POC Mutual Action Plan — environment sequencing, API keys & peering
messages:
From: Omar Salazar <omar.salazar@healthsync.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthSync IT <it@healthsync.ai>; procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — POC env prerequisites

Jordan — thanks for the call this morning. To keep momentum we need a concise mutual action plan that lists the sequence, owners, and dates for the POC environment handoff. Primary items we need you to commit to on your side: API key provisioning, org/tenant setup (for multi-team access), IP allowlist ranges, and the VPC peering window.

High level asks from our side: 
- Confirm minimal API key scope and how to rotate keys during POC.
- Provide a short checklist for org setup (teams, roles, audit logs).
- Share the exact IP ranges to allow on our firewall and any ephemeral IPs.
- Outline the VPC peering prerequisites and estimated maintenance window (we prefer a 2-hr window, PST).

Can you propose dates for the above next week? I’ve looped in our IT (it@healthsync.ai) and procurement for timing on contracts/SOW. I’ll attach our network diagram and provisional maintenance blackout windows.

Thanks,
Omar
Director of Engineering, HealthSync
attachments: healthsync-network-diagram.png

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Omar Salazar <omar.salazar@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC env prerequisites

Omar — appreciated the call. Drafted a compact MAP and attached a workbook (MAP_Redwood-HealthSync_v1.xlsx) that breaks the work into three sequential sprints with owners and target dates. Highlights below: 

Sprint A (Org + Keys) — target window: Jun 21–22
- Redwood owner: Jordan Blake (Account lead) — create org/tenant, invite HealthSync admin users, enable audit log retention (30d).
- Action: Issue scoped API keys for POC with least privilege (read/write for test endpoints only). Key rotation approach: short-lived API key + one-day rotation script (we’ll provide example).

Sprint B (Network Prep) — target window: Jun 23–24
- Redwood owner: Ben Carter (Solutions).
- Action: Confirm static egress IPs (list below), provide CIDR ranges for allowlisting. Coordinate with HealthSync IT for firewall rules.

Sprint C (Peering & Cutover) — target window: Jun 28 (2-hr maintenance window)
- Redwood owner: Neha Kapoor (Infra PM).
- Action: Perform VPC peering handshake, validate route tables, brief smoke tests. Fallback: if peering fails, route traffic to our hosted staging endpoint (no downtime for internal services).

Items we need from HealthSync to finalize dates: 
1) Confirmation of their internal owners for firewall changes and a proposed 2-hour maintenance window on Jun 28.
2) Procurement lead for SOW signoff so we can lock the peering window.

Quick notes on security/compliance: Keys will be scoped and logged; we’ll export audit logs daily and provide a read-only view for HealthSync. I attached the MAP workbook and linked the shared drive doc for live edits.

Next step: If the dates above look good, Ben will send the exact IP list and Neha will book the peering slot in our change calendar.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP_Redwood-HealthSync_v1.xlsx; link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=MAP_redwood_healthsync

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Omar Salazar <omar.salazar@healthsync.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC env prerequisites (IP ranges & peering notes)

Omar / Jordan — quick technical clarifications so HealthSync IT can plan firewall changes: 
- Redwood egress: we will provide a static set of four IPv4 addresses for the POC (34.203.12.45, 34.203.12.46, 34.203.12.47, 34.203.12.48). These will be used for API calls and callback webhooks.
- Ephemeral traffic: during large batch evals we may open additional ephemeral outbound ports — we will announce these 48 hours in advance and they are optional to allow.
- VPC peering prerequisites: healthsync must share a non-overlapping CIDR (e.g., 10.10.0.0/16) and create a route to our peering connection once established. We recommend pre-creating the peering resource on your side to speed the handshake.

Network test plan (recommended in the MAP workbook): 
1) Allowlist the four static IPs. 
2) Run a health-check script (we’ll provide) to confirm connectivity to the API endpoints.
3) Perform a controlled peer test during the window; validate route propagation and DNS resolution (we’ll handle the hostnames).

I attached a short network stub (healthsync-network-diagram.png referenced in the original). If you prefer, we can do a 30-min technical run-through with your network engineer before the peering day.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
attachments: healthsync-network-diagram.png

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Omar Salazar <omar.salazar@healthsync.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC env prerequisites (owners & timeline)

Team — marking owners and locking near-term milestones. Proposed concrete commitments: 
- Jun 21: Redwood creates tenant and issues API keys (Jordan to confirm once keys are generated).
- Jun 22: HealthSync IT confirms firewall rule changes (ticket number to be shared).
- Jun 23: Ben to deliver final IP whitelist and the health-check script.
- Jun 28, 09:00–11:00 PST: VPC peering handshake + smoke tests (Neha to lead).

Procurement note: procurement@healthsync.ai — we need a countersigned SOW to enable peering activity (network access requires the POC addendum). I’ve attached a draft SOW for review. If procurement can confirm by Jun 20, we’ll be able to proceed as scheduled.

If anyone needs to adjust windows, please flag by EOD Jun 18 so we can re-sequence Sprint B/C.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Infra Program Manager — Redwood Inference
attachments: draft-sow.pdf

From: Omar Salazar <omar.salazar@healthsync.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthSync IT <it@healthsync.ai>, procurement@healthsync.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC env prerequisites (confirming windows)

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our internal calendar. Confirming: 
- HealthSync IT will accept the four static IPs and open a ticket for firewall changes by Jun 22 (IT lead: Priya Rao, it@healthsync.ai).
- Procurement confirms receipt of draft SOW; we’ll aim for countersign by Jun 20 (procurement lead: procurement@healthsync.ai).
- We accept the Jun 28 09:00–11:00 PST peering window — please reserve a rollback plan and a short incident channel (we’ll use the #healthsync-redwood Slack channel).

I attached our updated network diagram with the CIDR we will use (10.10.0.0/16). We’ll schedule a 30-min tech prep with Ben on Jun 25 to run through the health-check script.

Appreciate the clear sequencing — Omar
Director of Engineering, HealthSync
attachments: healthsync-network-diagram.png
